title: The halo can leave the faces around the attachment point
subject: Whether the halo of an opened handle beyond distance 3 always lies on the faces around the attachment point
conclusion: On a ladder arm spliced onto a grid, at a junction point the frozen region of a port class runs along the arm's far long face with two-pattern claims, and the Fano plane and census 58 create there, off the faces around the attachment point; exact creation confirms this on a 21-point piece. So the halo lies on frozen lines whose claims survive the handle's single points, refuting PHASE-HALO's law of the faces around the point.
